title: Groups, broadcast lists, channels and communities

say: Groups, broadcast lists, channels and communities.
This is the video for module three of WhatsApp for Communication and Business.
WhatsApp gives you four ways to reach many people at once. Each one suits a different job, and choosing well saves everyone time.

say: A group is for conversation. Everyone sees and replies to every message. It can hold up to 1,024 members, good for teams, cooperatives and church departments.

panel.heading: Which tool does which job?
items: Group: members talk to each other, up to 1,024
Broadcast list: private copies, up to 256
Channel: one-way public updates
Community: many groups under one roof

say: A broadcast list sends the same message as a private copy to up to 256 contacts. They do not see each other, and replies come only to you.
But only people who saved your number receive it, so always ask new customers to save your number.

panel.heading: Which tool does which job?
items: Group: members talk to each other, up to 1,024
Broadcast list: private copies, up to 256
Channel: one-way public updates
Community: many groups under one roof

say: A channel, in the Updates tab, is a one-way public tool. Followers can react and vote in polls, but cannot reply, and phone numbers stay hidden on both sides.

say: A community links related groups, like branches, with one announcement group that reaches every member.

say: Mama Funke chairs a 60-member women's thrift cooperative, an ajo, in Ibadan. Their old group was full of forwarded videos, and members missed contribution reminders.
Step one. She creates a new group with a clear name, Bodija Women Ajo, and the cooperative's logo.

panel.heading: Set up a group like a careful admin
items: Clear name that says what it is for
Description with purpose and 3 to 5 rules
Edit group settings: admins only
Turn on Approve new members
Share the admin work; pin the payment warning

say: Step two. The description says: for contributions, meetings and loans only. No forwards, no adverts. Contributions due every Friday.

panel.heading: Set up a group like a careful admin
items: Clear name that says what it is for
Description with purpose and 3 to 5 rules
Edit group settings: admins only
Turn on Approve new members
Share the admin work; pin the payment warning

say: Step three. She sets Edit group settings to admins only, to stop pranks.

panel.heading: Set up a group like a careful admin
items: Clear name that says what it is for
Description with purpose and 3 to 5 rules
Edit group settings: admins only
Turn on Approve new members
Share the admin work; pin the payment warning

say: Step four. She turns on Approve new members, so strangers cannot slip in through the link. If a link gets into the wrong hands, Reset link stops it working.

panel.heading: Set up a group like a careful admin
items: Clear name that says what it is for
Description with purpose and 3 to 5 rules
Edit group settings: admins only
Turn on Approve new members
Share the admin work; pin the payment warning

say: Step five. She makes the treasurer and secretary admins, and pins the payment account details.
Scammers copy an admin's name and photo, then privately ask members to pay into a new account. So she pins this warning, and members confirm by phone with the treasurer before paying.

panel.rule: Account details never change by private message.

say: Uche sells foodstuff in bulk in Onitsha to about 400 regular buyers, and prices change often. One big group would expose every buyer's number and invite arguments.

panel.heading: Uche's weekly price update
right: Prices arrive as a private message
Replies come one by one to her

say: Instead she makes two broadcast lists of 200 contacts each, under the 256 limit. She asks every buyer to save her number.
Every Monday she sends this week's prices, marked approximate, call to confirm. Replies arrive privately, so she takes orders one by one.

say: Good group manners are simple. Stay on the group's purpose, reply to the exact message, and avoid posting between about 10pm and 6am except in emergencies. Never forward unverified health, security or money alerts.

cards.d: Reply to the exact message, send one complete message, and respect quiet hours.
A mention rings even if the group is muted. Use it only when you need that person.
Members vote with a tap and everyone sees the results.

say: Type the at sign and a name to mention someone. It reaches them even if they muted the group, so use it only when you truly need them.

say: To decide something, create a poll. Precious, secretary of a 90-member alumni group in Calabar, offered three dates. After 48 hours, 52 votes chose one date, with almost no extra messages.

say: Press and hold a busy group, tap mute, and choose 8 hours, 1 week or Always. Give your most important group its own tone, so you know it by sound.
Use the Unread and Groups filters to catch up quickly. And once a month, exit groups that no longer serve you, with a short polite thank-you.

panel.heading: Take back control
items: Mute busy, low-value groups
Custom tone for your key group
Use Unread and Groups filters
Exit groups you no longer need

say: To remember. Use a group to talk and a broadcast list for known contacts.
Use a channel for the public and a community for many branches.
Give every group a clear name, rules and admins-only settings. Pin the payment warning. And use polls for decisions and mute for noise.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Group to talk, broadcast to known contacts
Channel for the public, community for branches
Clear name, rules and admins-only settings
Pin the warning: accounts never change privately
Polls for decisions, mute for noise

say: Now practise. Create a small group with two or three trusted people and three rules. Build a broadcast list, mute five busy groups, and run a poll.
Then continue with the lessons below.
